newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sluggish NZ dollar ends on soft opening levels.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish NZ dollar ends on soft opening levels.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar barely moved during Monday's session and dealers said they were resigning themselves to a quiet period in the run-up to next week's government budget and major Reserve Bank statement.
By 5.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) the kiwi was squarely on its open of US$0.6885/92, against its finish last week at 0.6902/09. Dealers said it failed to venture out of a 10-point range during the day.
The Trade-Weighted Index showed more life, slipping to 67.65 from 67.72 at the open and down from 67.83 at Friday's close.
Its softness was largely the result of U.S. dollar weakness against the yen.
"I think we're coming into the inevitable holding pattern before the plethora of data next week," an Auckland dealer said.
The National/New Zealand First coalition government, formed in December after an inconclusive October general election, will present its first budget on June 26.
Hard on its heels comes the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's six-monthly Monetary Policy Statement on the morning of the 27th.
Dealers said that in the interim the kiwi was probably broadly in a 0.6880-6930 range, with the improved volume of eurokiwi issuance of late meaning the market was not too far away from finding bids.

However, it remained slightly vulnerable on the downside given the failure of the Australian unit to bounce back from last week's near one cent loss, which came after surprisingly weak employment data raised fears the Reserve Bank of Australia could ease official rates yet again.
Dealers said there was no reaction to data showing NZ's total overseas debt at NZ$75.5 billion at March 31, well below economists' average pick of $79.8 billion.
Forecasts for April retail trade data due on Tuesday range from a two percent fall to a five percent rise, with an average forecast of a 1.22 percent rise. Market reaction is expected to be muted.
